correctness.rationale: For \(n\ge4\), \(\theta>0\), each site \(2\le i\le n-1\), Féray's exact three-arrow partial-image identity gives an event mass \(\theta^r/D\) with r closed forced cycles. Counts of distinct loops, two-cycles, three-cycles and compatible disjoint pairs yield the displayed six coefficients with no missing cycle type; the six numerators sum to D. Their i-slopes are exactly 0, 1-theta^2, theta^2-1, theta^2-1, 1-theta^2, 0, proving rank-one site differences and exact finite-space total variation. The high-theta derivative has quartic Q with one sign change, \(Q(1)>0\) and negative leading coefficient, hence exactly one optimizer theta_n>1. At n=4 its high-theta maximum is below the unattained \(\theta\downarrow0\) limit; for n>=5 the explicit theta=n witness exceeds this limit by (n-1)[(n-5)^4+15(n-5)^3+72(n-5)^2+116(n-5)+18]>0. Scaling Q(cn)/n^4 gives -c(c-2)(c+1)^2, establishing \(\theta_n/n\to2\) and limiting maximal TV 8/27. Standalone rational verification passed 1270 assertions: all partial injection counts through n=12, full Ewens enumeration through n=8, and all-site TV. These finite tests are corroboration, not the proof.

originality.rationale: The identifiable prior general identities do not state the location-wise six-pattern probability vector, its exact one-dimensional positional contrast, or the sharp parameter-maximization phase change from n=4 to n>=5. The cycle-weighted partial-image formula, the joint peak-cycle generating function, and aggregate asymptotic limit laws are credited and excluded from the novelty claim. An earlier uniform fixed-point/consecutive-pattern covariance concerns a different weighting/statistic, and does not imply the present all-parameter site-to-site total variation. The strongest residual novelty risk is an undiscovered exact equivalent hidden in a general cycle-type generating identity or appendix.

value.rationale: The object is a natural six-symbol ordinal-pattern distribution in the classical Ewens random permutation model, and location bias matters for order-pattern statistics even though the law is conjugation-invariant. The theorem collapses all six local-site differences into one exact contrast, classifies the unique maximizer over parameter and sites (including the sharp exceptional n=4 nonattainment), and shows a macroscopic limiting maximal total variation of 8/27 at cycle bias \(\theta\sim2n\). These are quantitative structural and boundary facts not furnished by marginal peak expectations or routine normalization checks.
